commits.message:
feat(taxonomy): edit a candidate's term before approval, deterministic-first descriptions

Two gaps found while reviewing the taxonomy candidate queue: some
queued terms carry a parser artifact (stray punctuation, a fragment
that survived the "Required Skills" split) that a reviewer has no way
to fix short of rejecting the whole candidate and losing the
occurrence/sender history behind it. And every skill description was
an LLM call, even for the same handful of extremely common terms
(AWS, Docker, SAP, ...) that show up in almost every posting.

edit_taxonomy_candidate() (app/understanding/taxonomy/candidates.py)
lets a reviewer correct a pending candidate's term in place --
PATCH /taxonomy-candidates/{id}, wired into the "Taxonomy candidates"
table on the Blocklist & taxonomy page as an inline edit (same pattern
as the description editor on the Skills taxonomy page). Only ever
touches status='pending' rows; approving/rejecting afterward uses the
corrected term.

generate_skill_description() (descriptions.py) now checks a small
curated glossary of ~40 common terms first -- instant, free, and the
same wording every time the term comes up -- and only falls back to
the LLM for terms the glossary doesn't cover. Grow the glossary over
time as the same terms keep showing up in the review queue instead of
paying for an LLM call on every approval.

New coverage in the 900 suite: editing corrects the stored term and
its normalized_term, an empty edit is refused, an already-reviewed
candidate can't be edited, and a glossary term returns the curated
description instead of going through the LLM path. Full regression
suite (18 checks) green against a fresh schema and rebuilt image.
